comments.author: ahl
comments.html:
Capt. 69.238.229.71,

Indeed getting the time spent in each method or function would be useful -- and with DTrace it's trivial. All you have to do is record a timestamp (or vtimestamp) at each method or function entry, save it in a thread-local associative arrary, and print out the difference on the way out. In fact, this is a <em>very</em> common use of DTrace. Forgive me if it sounds trite, but I'll leave this as an exercise for the reader.

Mr. Benchmark,

Again, printing out timing information is easy because these java probes are first class citizens in the DTrace framework -- you can do all the usual DTrace-ish things with them. This example was with 1.5, and the agents should also work with 1.4.2 (and possibly earlier versions, but you're very much on your own there).

Adam
